facts.value: Key traits of the Irish genome have been present since the early Bronze Age, around 4,000 years ago.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: The world's highest frequencies of the R-L21 Y-chromosome haplotype and lactase persistence are found among people in Ireland.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: Haplogroup R1b is the dominant haplogroup among Irish males, reaching a frequency of almost 80%.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: R1b-L21 is the dominant sub-clade throughout Ireland, reaching a frequency of 65%.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: Modern Irish people have a small amount of ancestry from Early European Farmers and derive most of their ancestry from Western Steppe Herders.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: A recent archaeogenetics study found that the older Neolithic farming population was most similar to present-day Sardinians.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: Bronze Age men buried on Rathlin Island between 2000 and 1500 BC were most similar to present-day Irish people.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: The study indicates strong genetic continuity in Ireland from the Bronze Age to the modern era.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: The Bronze Age people of the R-L21 haplogroup likely brought the Bell Beaker culture to Ireland.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: It is suggested they also brought an Indo-European language that was an ancestor to the Insular Celtic and Gaelic languages.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: A 2017 genetic study shows that the Irish population can be divided into ten geographic genetic clusters.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: Seven clusters are of 'Gaelic' Irish ancestry, while three are of shared Irish-British ancestry.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: The largest difference is between native 'Gaelic' Irish populations and Ulster Protestants known to have recent, partial British ancestry.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: Irish people have most similarity to a 'Northwestern France' component and a 'West Norway' component related to the Viking era.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: Irish people have the least amount of Anglo-Saxon ancestry in the British Isles at around 10%.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: As of 2016, 10,100 Irish nationals of African descent referred to themselves as 'Black Irish' in the national census.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: The term 'Black Irish' is sometimes used outside Ireland to refer to Irish people with black hair and dark eyes.
facts.programme_association: Masters/PhD in Irish World Academy of Music and Dance

facts.value: One theory about 'Black Irish' descendants is that they come from Spanish traders or sailors of the Spanish Armada who were shipwrecked on Ireland's west coast, but there is little evidence for this.
